- If sentiment turns positive (≥0.67) within the last 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer for sharp drops or adjust downward bias.
- After a spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — apply “lag correction”: delay peak forecast by 1–2 days or reduce slope after sentiment spike.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day averages when sentiment is rising — use sentiment-weighted mean reversion: blend forecast with recent 7-day low if sentiment >0.67.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal after forecast peak, model exhibits “overconfidence lag” — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for each day after peak if sentiment drops below 0.67.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) for 5+ days, model tends to underestimate volatility — increase forecast variance or add 1–2% downward buffer for early days.
